why: A 310-clinic veterinary chain with about €565-595 million a year (roughly €1.8 million per clinic), matching the stated 'over €550 million', and gently moving indices is believable.
All four airline survey pies sum to 100% and the sample sizes and score spreads are plausible for passenger feedback.
Both spectator pies sum to 100% and 6,500 survey returns over three race meetings is plausible for a racing circuit.
Temporary packer hours stay below total hours every week and a doubling of orders and hours before Easter is believable for a chocolate maker.
A large-format sporting goods retailer with category revenues of 27-216 million and margins of 5-15% is believable.
Revenue minus costs matches the stated 12.8% and 6.9% margins, and about €20,000 a month on some 3,300-3,500 garments (about €6 each) fits a small dry cleaner.
Each faculty's postgraduate and undergraduate parts add to its printed total, and about 3.9 points a year of total enrolment growth is plausible for a university.
Revenue minus costs equals the stated profit in both periods, the average days per month match the calendar, and about $7 per case on 16-17 million cases a month is believable for a national bottler.
All four gym survey pies sum to 100% and the sample sizes and score spreads are plausible for a member poll.
About 2.8-2.9 watchmaker hours per full service, with 29 to 139 services a month, is believable, and the staffing (0.5 rising to 2.5 FTE) matches the step chart.
